title: Decide the AI Loot Designer: wire it into the loot module or delete it
body:
## Summary
The whole ai-designer folder (9 files, ~840 LOC) has zero importers in src, tests or e2e; AILootDesigner has never been mounted since it was written.

## Description
`src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/ai-designer/index.tsx:16` exports AILootDesigner; `git grep AILootDesigner` hits only its own definition, and `git log -G AILootDesigner` outside the component's own files is empty - no tab, route or test has ever rendered it. `src/lib/loot-designer/drop-simulator.ts` is consumed only by this folder plus two lib tests, so it is test-only reachable too. The context map describes an 'LLM-backed design pathway' that does not exist (no LLM call anywhere in the folder). Fixed looks like: either mount it as a loot sub-tab (direction: a capability the shipped UI does not offer) or delete the folder and decide the simulator's fate. Every other ai-designer card in this file is moot if it is deleted.

## Flow
- grep -rn AILootDesigner src e2e -> 1 hit (the definition)
- open the loot module: no tab reaches the designer
- operator chooses: mount (then land the ai-designer cards) or delete (then drop them)

## Expected impact
Designers either gain the drop-sim designer or the repo sheds ~840 unreachable LOC that sweeps keep polishing. Deleting breaks nothing reachable; mounting exposes the defects carded beside this one.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one decision ends maintenance of unreachable UI
Before: 0 importers of 9 files (grep); 0 renders in tests
After: mounted with >=1 test render, or 0 files
Method: probe - zero-consumer grep + git log -G; the decision itself is product direction
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
git grep -n AILootDesigner -> src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/ai-designer/index.tsx:16 only
git log --oneline -G AILootDesigner -- src (excluding the component's own files) -> (empty)
grep -rln loot-designer/drop-simulator src -> 6 ai-designer files + src/__tests__/lib/loot-designer/drop-simulator.test.ts + src/__tests__/lib/loot-drop-simulator.test.ts
instrument: operator decision; then a render test (mount) or the zero-importer grep (delete)

title: Claim Copied in the AI designer's UE5 code panel only after the write succeeds
body:
## Summary
CodePanel's Copy button sets 'Copied!' before navigator.clipboard.writeText resolves - the third loot Copy button; the other two were fixed in 065d7981.

## Description
`src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/ai-designer/CodePanel.tsx:14-18` calls `void navigator.clipboard.writeText(code)` then `setCopied(true)` and a raw `setTimeout(..., 1500)` with no unmount cleanup. A rejected write (insecure context, no focus) still shows Copied and leaves an unhandled rejection. 065d7981 moved EnemyLootBinding and LootTableEditor to the shared `copyToClipboard` (src/lib/clipboard.ts) + `UI_TIMEOUTS.copyFeedback`; this is the un-migrated pair. Gated on the ai-designer direction card (unreachable today).

## Flow
- Code tab -> Copy with writeText rejecting -> button reads Copied!
- fix: await copyToClipboard(code), return on false, UI_TIMEOUTS.copyFeedback
- extend src/__tests__/components/loot-copy-feedback.test.tsx with a CodePanel reject/resolve pair

## Expected impact
Users stop being told a copy happened when it did not. Nothing reachable can break (the panel is unmounted today).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - Copied only on a successful write
Before: 1 of 3 loot Copy buttons claims success unconditionally (grep)
After: 0 of 3; reject test green
Method: simulation - walked against 065d7981's identical fix; not built because the panel is unreachable (direction card)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: loot-copy-feedback.test.tsx CodePanel case: writeText rejects -> no 'Copied!'

title: Route the AI designer's affix eligibility through one minRarity rule
body:
## Summary
The minRarity eligibility rule exists three times: craftingKernel.isEligible (documented as the only copy), drop-simulator meetsRarity, and an inline indexOf in WeightTuning.

## Description
`src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/ai-designer/MetricsAndWeights.tsx:100` greys a slider with `RARITIES.indexOf(affix.minRarity) <= RARITIES.indexOf(rarity)` over its own `RARITIES` list (`src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/ai-designer/constants.ts:47`); the simulation it previews filters with `meetsRarity` over a private `RARITY_ORDER` (`src/lib/loot-designer/drop-simulator.ts:74,88`); docs/architecture/module-system.md:270 says craftingKernel's `isEligible` (`src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix-workbench/craftingKernel.ts:64`) is 'the only copy'. Three rarity orders, three predicates: a reordered or renamed tier can grey a slider the simulator still rolls. Fixed: export one predicate (lib) and have WeightTuning call it; the doc's 'only copy' claim then names its true scope. Touches lib + the affix-workbench sibling's file - out of scope this wave.

## Flow
- designer renders WeightTuning -> inline eligibility
- simulation -> meetsRarity
- fix: export meetsRarity (or reuse isEligible) and call it from WeightTuning; drop the local RARITIES

## Expected impact
The greyed sliders always match what the simulator can roll. Risk: none for current data (all three orders agree today).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one eligibility rule
Before: 3 predicates + 3 rarity orders (grep)
After: 1 predicate consumed by both
Method: simulation - the three walk identically on today's 5 tiers; a test feeding a reordered order would decide it
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/ai-designer/MetricsAndWeights.tsx:100
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/ai-designer/constants.ts:47
src/lib/loot-designer/drop-simulator.ts:74 const RARITY_ORDER
src/lib/loot-designer/drop-simulator.ts:88 function meetsRarity
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix-workbench/craftingKernel.ts:64 export function isEligible
instrument: render WeightTuning with a mocked predicate/order and assert the disabled set follows it

title: Show the AI designer's Level Scale from getItemLevelScaling, not a copy
body:
## Summary
LiveMetrics recomputes the item-level multiplier inline as 1 + 0.1*max(1, level) while the simulator it summarises uses getItemLevelScaling = 1 + 0.1*max(0, level).

## Description
`src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/ai-designer/MetricsAndWeights.tsx:23` prints `(1 + 0.1 * Math.max(1, itemLevel)).toFixed(1)x`; `src/lib/loot-designer/drop-simulator.ts:95` exports `getItemLevelScaling` with a max(0) clamp, documented as matching UE5 UARPGAffixRoller. They agree on the slider's range only because its min is 1 (`src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/ai-designer/DesignerPanel.tsx:141`). Fixed: import and print getItemLevelScaling(itemLevel). Gated on the direction card.

## Flow
- Designer tab -> Live Results -> Level Scale
- fix: GlowStat value = getItemLevelScaling(itemLevel).toFixed(1)

## Expected impact
The stat card can never disagree with the rolled magnitudes. Nothing reachable breaks.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one level-scaling rule
Before: 2 formulas (max(1) vs max(0)); 0 divergent outputs on 1..50
After: 1 formula
Method: probe - evaluated both over levels 0..50: differ only at 0 (1.1x vs 1.0x)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vi.mock getItemLevelScaling to a sentinel and assert LiveMetrics prints it

title: Name the generated GameplayEffect right in the AI designer's integration steps
body:
## Summary
CodePanel step 3 tells the user to create 'GE_OnEquip'; the code it sits under generates GE_<ItemName>_OnEquip.

## Description
`src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/ai-designer/CodePanel.tsx:51` hard-codes 'Create the GE_OnEquip GameplayEffect'; generateUE5Code in `src/lib/loot-designer/drop-simulator.ts` emits `// Create GE_<design.name>_OnEquip` (e.g. GE_FireSword_OnEquip). Fixed: build the step text from concept.name. Gated on the direction card.

## Flow
- Code tab -> Integration Steps -> step 3 says GE_OnEquip
- generated code above says GE_FireSword_OnEquip

## Expected impact
Following the steps produces the asset the code names. Nothing reachable breaks.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - steps match the generated code
Before: 1 of 5 steps names an asset the code does not
After: 0 of 5
Method: simulation - read both strings for the 6 presets; all 6 mismatch
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/ai-designer/CodePanel.tsx:51
src/lib/loot-designer/drop-simulator.ts generateUE5Code: '// Create GE_' + design.name + '_OnEquip with infinite duration'
instrument: render CodePanel for preset FireSword and assert step 3 contains GE_FireSword_OnEquip

title: Label the AI designer's Rarity and Rolls selects and expose its toggle states
body:
## Summary
DesignerPanel's Rarity and Rolls selects have no accessible name and suppress focus outlines; preset buttons and the More/Less toggle expose no pressed/expanded state.

## Description
`src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/ai-designer/DesignerPanel.tsx:127-135` and `:151-158`: the visible 'Rarity'/'Rolls' text is a sibling span, not a label, and the selects carry no aria-label, with `focus:outline-none` and no `.focus-ring`; the Level range beside them is labelled (`:143`). Preset buttons (`:57-74`) show selection only by colour (no aria-pressed); `src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/ai-designer/MetricsAndWeights.tsx:88-91` More/Less has no aria-expanded. Gated on the direction card.

## Flow
- keyboard-tab into Rarity select -> no visible focus, announced as an unnamed combobox
- fix: aria-label (or label htmlFor), focus-ring, aria-pressed on presets, aria-expanded on More/Less

## Expected impact
Keyboard and screen-reader users can operate the designer. Nothing reachable breaks.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every control named and its state exposed
Before: 2 unnamed selects, 2 outline-suppressed, 6 presets + 1 toggle without state
After: 0 / 0 / 0
Method: simulation - DOM read of the JSX; a render test querying role+name would decide it
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: render DesignerPanel; assert getByRole('combobox',{name:/rarity/i}) and aria-pressed/aria-expanded

title: Derive the AI designer's 'deployed' count instead of hard-coding 4/4
body:
## Summary
The designer's TabHeader always reads '4/4 deployed' - a constant, while the other core-engine TabHeaders derive implemented/total from feature status.

## Description
`src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/ai-designer/index.tsx:76-77` passes `implemented={4} total={4}`; TabHeader (`src/components/modules/core-engine/unique-tabs/_shared/headers.tsx:63`) paints it success-green as complete. `src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/index.tsx:70`, sub_ability and sub_combat derive `stats.implemented/total`. Fixed: derive from feature status, or drop the counter. Gated on the direction card.

## Flow
- render AILootDesigner -> header '4/4 deployed' in success green regardless of state

## Expected impact
A completeness claim stops being unconditional. Nothing reachable breaks.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the header claims only what is measured
Before: 1 hard-coded completion claim; 6 sibling headers derive theirs (grep implemented=)
After: 0 hard-coded
Method: probe - grep of implemented= across core-engine: 1 literal of 7
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: render AILootDesigner and assert the header count follows its source

title: Derive the loot treemap's probabilities from RARITY_TIERS, not a second copy
body:
## Summary
TREEMAP_DATA.probability hand-repeats RARITY_TIERS' weights (50/25/15/8/2), so three Feature Map glyphs show one split from two hand-maintained lists.

## Description
`src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/_shared/data.ts:89-95` TREEMAP_DATA probabilities 50/25/15/8/2 duplicate `src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/_shared/data.ts:40-46` RARITY_TIERS weights; the Weights and Histogram glyphs read RARITY_TIERS, the Treemap glyph reads TREEMAP_DATA (`src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/metrics/TreemapMetric.tsx:9`). Edit one and the Feature Map shows two rarity splits. _shared belongs to loot-affix-core - out of scope this wave.

## Flow
- change a RARITY_TIERS weight -> Weights/Histogram move, Treemap does not
- fix: TREEMAP_DATA probability = tier weight share (or build TREEMAP_DATA from RARITY_TIERS + affix lists)

## Expected impact
The three rarity-split glyphs cannot disagree. Risk: Treemap tooltips change if weights ever stop summing to 100.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one source for the rarity split
Before: 2 hand-maintained lists, 5 duplicated numbers
After: 1 list
Method: probe - diffed the two arrays: 5/5 values identical by hand
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Align the Feature Map's Pipeline card description with the drawn pipeline stages
body:
## Summary
The arpg-loot Pipeline card describes 'Roll → rarity → affix → drop flow' while its glyph and the metrics view name LootTable → WeightedRandom → WorldItem → Pickup → Inventory.

## Description
`src/components/modules/core-engine/unique-tabs/feature-map-config.ts:125` g('Core','pipeline',...,'Roll → rarity → affix → drop flow'); `src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/metrics/lootMetricsView.ts` LOOT_PIPELINE_STAGES is the 5-stage list the glyph draws and its tooltip names (df3ff028 removed the view's copy of the old phrase). The card's text and its glyph describe different pipelines. feature-map-config is outside this context.

## Flow
- open the loot Feature Map -> Pipeline card text vs hover tooltip disagree
- fix: derive the description from LOOT_PIPELINE_STAGES or rewrite it to the same 5 stages

## Expected impact
One pipeline description on the card. Nothing breaks.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - card copy and glyph agree
Before: 2 descriptions of one pipeline
After: 1
Method: simulation - read both strings
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: test asserting the pipeline section description mentions every LOOT_PIPELINE_STAGES entry (owner: unique-tabs context)
